    "title": "Python on Windows: reserved device names bypass basename sanitization and cause silent data loss",
    "content": "When accepting user-supplied filenames for file I/O on Windows, `os.path.basename()` does not filter Windows reserved device names (CON, NUL, COM1–COM9, LPT1–LPT9). For example, `os.path.basename('NUL')` returns `'NUL'`, which passes typical empty-string fallback checks. Calling `open('NUL.json', 'w')` then silently writes to the null device — the data is discarded without any error or exception.
